acceptance_criteria.given: A approved with a commit that conflicts with B's committed work on f.txt
acceptance_criteria.then: B's checkout is not mid-merge, B's f.txt is unchanged, and B's prompt contains git merge --no-ff <A's sha>, A's task id and f.txt

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing checkout with uncommitted changes and a missing approved prerequisite
acceptance_criteria.then: the changes are committed by an auto-snapshot, the prerequisite is merged and the turn starts
acceptance_criteria.when: a turn is bound to the task

acceptance_criteria.given: a checkout left mid-merge on an approved prerequisite commit with unresolved conflicts
acceptance_criteria.then: the end-of-turn snapshot does not commit the conflicted merge and the next turn starts with a note saying the merge is unfinished
acceptance_criteria.when: the turn ends and the next turn is bound to the task

acceptance_criteria.given: an approved prerequisite's commit conflicts with commits already on the dependent's branch
acceptance_criteria.then: the merge is abandoned, the branch tip and working files are unchanged, and the turn starts with the merge instruction

acceptance_criteria.given: B's branch lacks approved prerequisite A's commit
acceptance_criteria.then: first 409 naming A and its commit with detail.unmerged_prerequisites[].commit_sha; then approval succeeds
acceptance_criteria.when: B is approved, then approved again after the author merges, resolves and commits

design: D1 resolve_turn_workspace returns (path, notes); notes are re-derived from the repository so the prompt describes the checkout as it is. D2 Clean handover, not mid-merge, because a mid-merge checkout is refused by ensure_task_worktree. D3 The gate and the notice share unmerged_prerequisites. No migration.

problem: worktrees._catch_up_prerequisites refused every turn on a dependent task whose checkout conflicted with an approved prerequisite's commit. The refusal said to run git merge --no-ff, which is the author's work, but the author never got a turn; only the operator could fix it by hand (sweep 2026-10-18, group C).

requirements.rationale: A checkout seeded only at creation keeps whatever prerequisites happened to be approved then; the existing branch holds the task's own work, so the catch-up never destroys it. Reconciling two pieces of work is the author's job: refusing the turn left the author no turn to do it and only the operator could fix it by hand (F695), while a conflict with main was already the agent's to resolve in its own turn.
requirements.statement: When a turn is bound to a task whose checkout already exists, the Hub SHALL first merge in the commit of each approved prerequisite the branch does not contain, without discarding anything. A conflicting approved prerequisite is abandoned with the checkout left clean, the turn starts with a merge instruction naming the prerequisite task, commit and conflicting paths, and approval is refused until the task's branch contains the commit; uncommitted changes are snapshotted before the catch-up rather than refused; a checkout mid-merge on an approved prerequisite commit is handed back with a note rather than refused, and a merge with unresolved conflicts is never auto-committed. A merge that does not finish in time SHALL abort the merge, leave the branch and files as they were, and refuse the turn with a message naming the prerequisite, its commit, the checkout and the merge command.

requirements.rationale: Repeated turns on one task must not rebuild it, and a dependent started before its prerequisite was approved must not go on without that work. The existing branch carries the task's own work, so nothing may be rewritten. A conflict is the author's to merge (F695): the turn starts with the instruction and approval waits for the commit. A task released and worked again is re-provisioned from its retained branch, so it resumes with its prior work.
requirements.statement: Provisioning a task checkout that already exists, correctly registered for its branch, SHALL return it without rebuilding it and SHALL then merge in, as merge commits, the commits of the task's approved prerequisites that its branch lacks. A conflicting approved prerequisite is abandoned with the checkout left clean and handed to the turn's author with a merge instruction, uncommitted changes are snapshotted before the catch-up, and a merge that does not finish in time SHALL refuse the turn and leave the branch tip and files unchanged.

requirements.rationale: One implementation: the gate runs the same unmerged_prerequisites function the turn's notice is derived from, against refs/heads/<task branch>.
requirements.statement: Moving a task with its own checkout to approved SHALL be refused while any approved prerequisite's commit is not contained in the task's branch; the refusal (gate_unsatisfied, category unmerged_prerequisites) SHALL name the prerequisite task and commit.

in_scope: the turn notice carrying the merge instruction
non_goals: Merging the prerequisite for the author

summary: When an approved prerequisite conflicts with a dependent task's existing checkout, the Hub abandons the merge, starts the author's turn with a merge instruction, and refuses approval until the task's branch contains the prerequisite's commit (F695).
title: A conflicting prerequisite is the author's to merge
